message.content:
The last common ancestor of a lion (Panthera leo) and a zebra (Equus quagga) is the last common ancestor of all placental mammals (Eutheria).  
That ancestor lived roughly 100 – 110 million years ago, before the split that led to the two distinct mammalian lineages that eventually gave rise to the carnivoran (lion) and perissodactyl (zebra) orders.
